definitions.explanation: A job or career that requires specialized knowledge, training, or qualifications, such as law, medicine, engineering, or accounting.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{専門職|せんもんしょく}として{働|はたら}いている。
{専門職|せんもんしょく}に{就|つ}くには{資格|しかく}が{必要|ひつよう}な{場合|ばあい}が{多|おお}い。
examples.english: Qualifications are often required to enter a professional occupation.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}や{弁護士|べんごし}などの{専門職|せんもんしょく}は{社会的|しゃかいてき}な{信頼|しんらい}が{高|たか}い。
examples.english: Professional occupations such as doctors and lawyers enjoy high social trust.

notes:
A compound of {専門|せんもん} (specialty; specialization) and {職|しょく} (occupation; job). Refers to careers that demand advanced education, specialized training, or professional certification. In Japanese labor classification, {専門職|せんもんしょく} is a distinct category from {総合職|そうごうしょく} (general career track) and {一般職|いっぱんしょく} (clerical track).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {専門職|せんもんしょく}に{就|つ}く: to enter a professional occupation
- {専門職|せんもんしょく}{大学院|だいがくいん}: professional graduate school
- {高度|こうど}{専門職|せんもんしょく}: highly specialized profession
- {専門職|せんもんしょく}{学位|がくい}: professional degree

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {専門家|せんもんか}: specialist; expert — refers to the person, not the job category
- {技術職|ぎじゅつしょく}: technical position — specifically about engineering or technical work
- {総合職|そうごうしょく}: general career track — the management track in Japanese companies, contrasted with {専門職|せんもんしょく}
